gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Creality Falcon A1C, ChatGPT's budget pick, engraves a 150 × 150 mm bed (34.9 sq in). That is about one-sixth of the xTool M2 10W's 426 × 320 mm bed (211.3 sq in), so the A1C costs $7.71 per sq in of bed at $269 against $2.36 for the M2 at $499.
standout_why: maker-wise.com (cited) prints prices and some work areas but no price per square inch or per watt. For the xTool M2 it says only 'check spec sheet', and it does not cover the Falcon A1 or A1C at all. Tom's Hardware (cited) and the xTool beginner guide (cited) returned only their titles through my fetch tool: Tom's text was 120 characters and xTool's was cut off after the title. I could not see whether they give bed sizes, so I scored this a 2 rather than a 3.
decides: This changes the budget advice. ChatGPT calls the A1C a 'smaller work area', but for $230 more ($269 vs $499) the M2 10W gives about 6× the bed. That means a beginner pays roughly 1.9× the price for 6× the usable area. So the A1C is only the right pick when the shopper's projects fit in a 5.9 in square, such as coasters, tags and keychains. Price per watt doesn't separate the 10 W and 20 W picks: the M2 10W is $49.90/W, the Falcon A1 10W $54.90/W and the A1 Pro 20W $54.95/W. Bed size per dollar is the figure that differs.
